newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea opens two new nuclear power stations.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea opens two new nuclear power stations.

text.p: South Korea on Saturday opened its 10th and 11th nuclear power stations and broke ground for two more, state-owned Korea Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) said.

With the two 1,000-megawatt units up and running, nuclear power now represents 26.9 percent of South Korea's total annual power generation capacity of 35.702 megawatts, the utility said in a statement.
Construction of the stations, located in the southern coast city of Youngkwang, began in June 1989. The units cost a total of 2.83 trillion won ($3.42 billion), KEPCO added.
KEPCO subsidiary Korea Power Engineering Co designed the stations and state-run Korea Heavy Industries and Construction Corp manufactured the reactors and turbine systems, it said.
South Korea's Hyundai Engineering and Construction Co was the main contractor.
Ground was broken also on Saturday for two new stations, also to be located in Youngkwang.

One is scheduled for completion by 2001 and the other by the following year at a combined cost of 3.22 trillion won, KEPCO said. Daelim Industrial Co and Hyundai are the main contractors for construction of the new units, it added.
